key_insight: Mobile ions have only a small effect on steady-state efficiency in efficient perovskite solar cells, with their impact strongly dependent on device parameters such as ion density, recombination, and band offsets.
engineering_relevance: For device design, this suggests that optimizing interfaces and recombination losses may matter more than suppressing ion motion in already high-performing perovskite solar cells.
method: Drift-diffusion modeling of perovskite solar cells
Factorial analysis across key materials and device parameters
Paired comparison of 601 matched cell pairs (1202 total), with and without mobile ions
evidence_signal: The study systematically simulated 601 paired devices over a broad physically relevant parameter range to isolate the effect of mobile ions on steady-state performance.
watch_item: Results are based on modeled steady-state behavior, so transient effects, degradation, and real-device defect complexity may not be fully captured.
paper_title: An Investigation into the Effect of Mobile Ions on the Steady State Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
